Using the New Call Center Phone Menu

Oct 14, 2026

As previously communicated, on October 12, MaineCare launched a new interactive voice response (IVR) system, Gabby, to enhance the provider self-service experience and help callers to Provider Services access information more quickly and efficiently. 

Gabby can assist with five common inquiry types: 

  • Claim Status 
  • Prior Authorizations 
  • Member Eligibility
  • Payments
  • Provider Enrollment 

When you call, simply tell Gabby which of these topics best matches your reason for calling. Depending on your inquiry, Gabby will ask for basic information, such as your NPI, Tax ID, or a member ID, to verify your request. Please have this information ready before you call so that you can quickly provide it to Gabby. Gabby will prompt multiple times for the information it needs to proceed. If you do not provide a valid response, Gabby will disconnect. 

Once your information is validated, Gabby will guide you through additional prompts to help you obtain the information you need. 

If your inquiry is not related to one of the self-service options listed above, tell Gabby "other" to connect with a customer service representative for further assistance. You can ask to speak to customer service representative or agent at any time. 

In addition, to give providers expanded time for support, on Thursday, October 15, 2026, the Call Center will be open until 7:00 PM. 

As a reminder, in addition to calling Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585, you can also email MaineCareprovider@gainwelltechnologies.com. For MaineCare Partner Portal issues, you can email MaineCaresupport@gainwelltechnologies.com.

item.description: Thursday, October 15, 2026 The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF. At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. Additionally, the following websites are unavailable: bnc.uscourts.gov bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov notices.uscourts.gov National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.

item.title: US Department of Labor awards more than $10.5M in grants to support mine safety, health training across the nation
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor announced today that its Mine Safety and Health Administration has awarded more than $10.5 million in grants to reduce mining accidents, injuries, and illnesses by supporting training and education programs.The agency is awarding these grants to support the delivery of federally mandated training for new and experienced miners at surface and underground coal and metal and nonmetal mines. MSHA is awarding grants in 45 states, the Navajo Nation, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership we’re investing billions of dollars into critical mining projects and resources for mining education,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Today’s grant announcement furthers the Department’s goal to expand mining across the United States to support this Administration’s goals to provide critical resources to the workers industries that continue to expand in America.”States and territories apply for grant funding, which is then awarded to state mine inspectors’ offices, state departments of labor, and state-supported colleges and universities. item.title: Hours of Service of Drivers: Association of American Railroads and American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association; Application for Exemption Renewal
item.description: FMCSA announces its final decision to renew and modify the exemption granted to the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association and member railroads (the Associations) from the hours-of-service (HOS) prohibitions against driving after the 14th hour after coming on duty (the 14-hour rule) and against driving after accumulating 60 hours of on duty time within 7 consecutive days, or 70 hours of on duty time within 8 consecutive days (the 60-hour/70-hour rule). The exemption will enable covered drivers to respond to unplanned events that occur outside of, or extend beyond, their normal work hours. FMCSA modifies the previous exemption to limit the categories of unplanned events during which the exemption may be used and to add reporting requirements. In addition, only drivers operating for motor carriers listed in the Appendix to this decision may operate under the exemption. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and has determined that the exemption renewal, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.

item.title: US Department of Labor awards $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago Grants to promote mine safety, health education
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $250,000 in Brookwood-Sago grant funding to two organizations to support education and training initiatives that will help identify and prevent unsafe working conditions in and around the nation’s mines.Administered by the department’s Mine Safety and Health Administration, the Brookwood-Sago Mine Safety grant program helps recipients create training materials, conduct mine safety training, and educational programs designed to protect the safety and health of miners. In awarding the grants, MSHA focused on innovative plans for mine safety and pilot programs that may be useful for miners working in a broad range of positions. The grants also put an emphasis on programs and materials targeting workers in smaller mines that train mine operators and miners about MSHA standards, and emergency response training.Established under the Mine Improvement and New Emergency Response Act of 2006, the grant program honors the miners lost at the Jim Walter Resources #5 mine in Brookwood, Alabama, on Sept. 23, 2001, and at the Sago Mine in Buckhannon, West Virginia, on Jan. 2, 2006.The recipients of the 2026 Brookwood-Sago grants are as follows:RecipientCityState/TerritoryAmountSaelua Medical Corporation Pago PagoAmerican Samoa$170,000University of ArizonaTucsonAZ$80,000

item.title: US Department of Labor obtains consent order against retirement plan fiduciaries of defunct Chicago law firm for failing to distribute $6.4M in assets
item.description: CHICAGO – Following a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Labor, a defunct Chicago law firm’s retirement plan distributed $6,498,858 in retirement plan assets to 40 employees. The plan’s fiduciaries failed to properly terminate the plan and disburse those funds as required by law.On Aug. 18, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, entered a consent order resolving the department’s claims against the McCullough, Campbell & Lane LLP, and the firm’s capital partners David L. Joslyn, John W. McCullough, F. Dennis Nelson, and Paul S. Turner. The department alleged that the defendants violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act by failing to follow a 2019 partnership resolution. The resolution required them to terminate the firm’s retirement plan and distribute the plan’s assets to employees. The defendants have provided proof that plan’s assets were distributed to participants, except for approximately $13,861 in the employer-level plan accounts. The consent order requires the plan’s recordkeeper to distribute those funds to its participants and to terminate the plan. “After their law firm closed, Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn failed to provide employees with their promised retirement benefits,” said Employee Benefits Security Administration Regional Director Kelli Hammerl in Chicago. “The Department of Labor helped participants gain access to their retirement savings.” The order permanently bars Turner, McCullough, Nelson, and Joslyn from serving as fiduciaries or service providers for any ERISA-covered employee benefit plan.
